subject: which encounter model for live trapping data?

messages.author: a215fdd0ac20af41
messages.subject: which encounter model for live trapping data?
parts:
Hello Everyone,
I have a live-trapping dataset for voles, and I'm wondering which encounter model to use.

The issue is that once a trap is occupied, it's not available for others to occupy. I have a note from Chris from the SMBI workshop this summer that I should use encmod=M. However when I read the documentation it sounds like this is used mainly when you have the chance of capturing more than 1 individual in each trap, which isn't my situation.

Chris and others, what would you recommend?

I should add that I'm not sure how necessary it is to correct for this, based on what I'm reading in the literature. Our trap checks were every 8 hours, traps were pretty close together (every 10m), and trap saturation was low enough (on average 4.5 traps occupied per 100 traps available each check) that we might not need to worry about this. Does anyone else have experience or thoughts on this issue?

Thanks for the help! Karen

messages.author: 58a62321f08f30f8
messages.subject: Re: [oscr] which encounter model for live trapping data?
parts:
Hi Karen,

Based on the situation you describe (check frequency and saturation), the 'multicatch' model should be absolutely fine.

You can convince yourself of this but reading this nice paper by Greg Distiller and David Botchers:

A spatially explicit capture–recapture estimator for single‐catch traps

https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ece3.1748
